newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela foreign reserves fall to $15.184 bln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela foreign reserves fall to $15.184 bln.

text.p: Venezuela's total foreign reserves fell $220 million, or 1.4 percent, in the week to December 23 to $15.184 billion, according to new figures released by the central bank.
Reserves were down from $15.404 billion on December 16, the bank's latest weekly bulletin of indicators showed.
Last week the Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) said it paid $250 million in overdue debt to the Paris Club.

On Thursday, the Central Bank said it expected foreign reserves to end the year at $15.133 billion -- up from 1995's close of $9.723 billion. That rise, largely thanks to higher than expected international oil prices, exceeds IMF-agreed targets for a $1.5 billion increase by year-end.
The sustained rise has complicated monetary policy, government officials have said, increasing liquidity.
